crime_highlights: The three acosted and assaulted Mr. Gormley until he lay prostrate and helpless on the pathway.
Mr. Edwards continued his attack with additional kicks and stomps to the head of Mr. Gormley.
Actual death was caused during this portion of the attack by a kick to the temple.
the beating left Mr. Gormley's head a bloody, pulpy and nearly unrecognizable mass
rationale_highlights: Mr. Edwards is a native person with a very deprived upbringing.
Many trace much of the cause to the identity-and-culture-destroying residential school system to which his grandparents were subjected.
Considering the principles outlined in Gladue and Courtereille, I will fix that period at twelve years.
note: Gladue reduced parole ineligibility from fourteen to twelve years.

crime_highlights: the accused received from the Band the sum of approximately $140,000.00
I found that the accused, Hazel Wilson, and or, someone on her behalf, prepared false documents to support these payments
I also found that the accused falsified some of the forms that were used to determine eligibility for social assistance
some endorsements on some of the cheques that were issued were forged
rationale_highlights: I must consider not only s. 718.2(e) and its interpretation by the Supreme Court of Canada in Gladue and Wells, supra, due to the accused's aboriginal heritage, but also the presence of a number of mitigating factors
note: Court never states clearly the effect of aboriginal status on sentence.

crime_highlights: a violent fight between a slight, peaceable young man and the two accused, one of whom outweighs the deceased nearly two to one
The fight left the deceased dead and the kitchen covered in the deceased's blood.
After the killing, Brandon Christophersen's body was dismembered and disposed of.
rationale_highlights: I must consider the sentencing purpose of rehabilitation, s. 718(d), a minimal depravation of liberty under s. 718.2(d) and (e), as well as the fact both accused are of First Nations ancestry
keeping in mind their youth, their aboriginal background and the length of time that they will serve prior to being eligible for parole
note: Aboriginal background only mentioned as a consideration; no systemic discussion or stated effect.
